Read out of saint.gr's line for 8 Φεβρουαρίου, «Προφήτης Ζαχαρίας», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the name link behind days.pravoslavie.ru's line for 8 февраля ст. ст., «Захария Серповидец, пророк, из 12 малых пророков», with the rank word and the note of his place among the twelve left off. «Серповидец» — the sickle-seer — is the calendar's own by-name, after the flying sickle of his fifth vision, and is kept with the name.

floruit.note: As printed by days.pravoslavie.ru: «Прор. Захарии Серповидца из 12-ти (ок. 520 до Р.Х.).» Recorded as a floruit, the shape malachi holds for the same kind of bracket.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 8 февраля ст. ст. — «Прор. Захарии Серповидца из 12-ти (ок. 520 до Р.Х.).»
Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 8 februarie — «Sfântul Proroc Zaharia»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 8ης Φεβρουαρίου — «Προφήτης Ζαχαρίας»

Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 21.02.2026 (8. фебруар ст. ст.) — „2. Свети пророк Захарија. Једанаести од мањих пророка. Заједно с пророком Агејем побуђивао кнеза Зоровавеља да обнови храм јерусалимски. … Упокојио се последње године царовања Дарија Хистаспа, око 520. године пре Христа.“

attestations.note: Read from the Prologue text on the page, not from its entry list; he is its second numbered entry and the list printed his heading. It is the only one of the four to number him among the minor prophets — the eleventh — and to say what he and Haggai did, which was to urge the prince Zerubbabel to rebuild the temple at Jerusalem. It cites three of his prophecies by chapter and verse and explains his epithet: he is called the Sickle-seer because he saw in a vision a sickle coming down from heaven to mow the unrighteous, and thieves and blasphemers of God's name especially. Its year of repose, «око 520. године пре Христа», agrees with the Russian line's «(ок. 520 до Р.Х.)», which was cited on this folder and had never been recorded as a date; the folder carried no dates at all before this batch. The Prologue sets the same repose in the last year of the reign of Darius Hystaspes, and no source read here gives that reign's years, so the quoted words stand in the note and nothing is computed from them.

hymns.text: A prorocului Tău, Doamne, Zaharia pomenire prăznuind, printr-însul Te rugăm, mântuieşte sufletele noastre.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Proroc Zaharia, Glasul 2

english.text: Keeping the memorial of Thy prophet Zacharias, O Lord, through him we entreat Thee: save our souls.

hymns.text: Τὴν κλῆσιν κατάλληλον, δείξας τοὶς ἔργοις σοφέ, ταμεῖον ἐπάξιον, τῆς ἐπιπνοίας Θεοῦ, Ζαχαρία γεγένησαι, ἔχων γὰρ ἐν τῷ βίῳ, συλλαλούντας Ἀγγέλους, ὤφθης τῶν ἐσομένων, θεηγόρος Προφήτης. Καὶ νῦν ἠμῶν τᾶς αἰτήσεις, ἄνωθεν πλήρωσαν.

source.text: Ορθόδοξος Συναξαριστής (saint.gr) — Προφήτης Ζαχαρίας, Λειτουργικά κείμενα: Ἀπολυτίκιον

english.text: Having shown your name to fit your works, wise Zacharias, you became a treasury worthy of the inbreathing of God; for having angels to talk with you in your life, you were shown a God-speaking prophet of the things to come. And now fulfil our askings from above.

death.note: Two sources, one figure, and it had never been recorded: this folder carried no dates although the year was quoted in its own Russian citation. days.pravoslavie.ru for 8 февраля ст. ст.: «Прор. Захарии Серповидца из 12-ти (ок. 520 до Р.Х.).»; the Ohrid Prologue at pravoslavno.rs for the Julian 8 February: „Упокојио се последње године царовања Дарија Хистаспа, око 520. године пре Христа.“ The Prologue also puts the repose in the last year of Darius Hystaspes's reign; no source read here gives that reign's years, so its words are quoted and no year is derived from them. saint.gr and doxologia.ro give no year.
